info.name: Miqaat Identity Federation
info.description:
## Run order
1. **1. Sign in**, top to bottom. `Portal page` saves `transaction_id` + `csrf`; `POST /login` saves the CORE `role_id`; the two `select-scope` requests save `access_token` (Authorization API) and `admin_identity_access_token` (Identity admin). Both are also stored as globals `access_token` / `identity_access_token`, which the *Miqaat Core Identity Authorization* collection uses.
2. **2. Client administration** after changing a client in the Authorization collection.
3. **3. Embedded login**: `Create transaction` (saves the CSRF token) → `Authenticate` (saves `core_assertion` and `sid`). `Transaction status` shows PENDING/COMPLETED; `Embedded login page` is only needed when the API does not return the token (production).
4. **5. Business unit app (RMS reference)**: RMS start → Identity login page → Identity sign in → RMS callback → `/api/me` shows the claims stored in the encrypted `rms_session` cookie. Needs a user with an RMS role.

## CSRF
Browser endpoints (`/login`, `/select-scope`, `/portal/*`, `/embed/*`) need `Origin: {{identity}}` (exactly: `localhost`, not `127.0.0.1`) and `X-CSRF-Token` from the page boot JSON, with the matching `transaction_id`. These requests send both. The pair is valid for 5 minutes before sign-in; after a portal sign-in it is bound to that session for the session lifetime. On `403 CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `details.reason` says why: re-run `Portal page` (or `Embedded login page`).

## Cookies and secrets
Postman's cookie jar keeps `federation_session` for localhost. `401 SESSION_REQUIRED` means it is missing: run `POST /login` again or check Cookies → localhost. Put `password` in the *current value* only so it is never exported.

item.name: 1. Sign in (portal, CSRF, tokens)
item.description: Run top to bottom. Variables are filled by the test scripts.

exec: pm.test('login page boot JSON found', () => pm.expect(m, 'no boot JSON: read the HTML error page in the response').to.not.equal(null));

request.description: Same as POST /portal/login. Returns every workspace; with exactly one it is activated and a scoped token is returned. Non-ITS: "identity_type": "NON_ITS", "identifier": "<email>".
Same as /portal/select-scope; also Switch Workspace. Needs the session cookie + CSRF. Token for the Authorization API (port 3002).
Token for Identity admin endpoints: client refresh (CONFIGURATION edit) and force logout (USER_MGMT edit).
Workspaces of the signed-in session.
Applications the user can launch in PORTAL_ENVIRONMENT.
Same handler as POST /login (the portal page uses this path). Use instead of POST /login: run Portal page first, since a transaction signs in only once.
Same handler as POST /select-scope; also Switch Workspace from the portal page.

item.name: 2. Client administration
item.description: Apply origin, callback or status changes made in the Authorization service immediately.

request.description: CORE workspace with CONFIGURATION edit, token audience identity. Returns the reloaded status, allowed_embed_origins and callback_uris. Send no Content-Type (empty body).

item.name: 3. Embedded login
item.description: What a BU application does. Transactions are single use and expire after 5 minutes: run Create transaction again for each try.

request.description: Fresh client configuration: origin is one of the registered origins (required when the client has several). Saves transaction_id, login_url and csrf (returned outside production). 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED: add the origin to the client. 403 CLIENT_NOT_ACTIVE: activate the client.
PENDING or COMPLETED, bound target_origin and expires_in. Never returns the CSRF token.

item.name: Embedded login page (optional: saves embed_csrf from HTML)

exec: pm.test('login page boot JSON found', () => pm.expect(m, 'no boot JSON: read the HTML error page in the response').to.not.equal(null));

request.description: The iframe page. Only needed when TRANSACTION_API_RETURNS_CSRF is off (production): its boot JSON carries the CSRF token.

Returns MIQAAT_AUTH_SUCCESS with core_assertion (RS256, 60 s, single use) and sets federation_session. The test script saves core_assertion and its sid claim and logs the decoded claims to the Postman console.
Needs a fresh, unused transaction and an existing federation_session: run Create transaction + Embedded login page first.

item.name: Portal sign out, this browser (scope session)

request.description: Revokes the session and sends logout+jwt to every application that received an assertion.
CORE workspace with USER_MGMT edit, audience identity. Returns revoked_sessions and clients_notified.

item.name: Force logout a session by sid (administrator)
Federation logout, browser form from an application

request.description: Reference only: a real browser sends it as a top-level form with the federation cookie. 303 to the registered post-logout URI.

item.name: 5. Business unit app (RMS reference, :4001)
item.description: The complete embedded login as an application performs it: start in RMS, sign in on Identity, hand the assertion to the RMS backend, then use the app. Postman keeps the rms_login_txn and rms_session cookies for localhost:4001. Needs a user with an RMS role (e.g. 30337752); otherwise the callback returns 403 ACCESS_DENIED:APPLICATION_ACCESS_DENIED.

item.name: RMS: start login (saves transaction, state, login_url)

request.description: The transaction is bound to the Origin header (any origin registered for rms-web-dev) and to this cookie jar (rms_login_txn).

item.name: Identity: login page for RMS (saves embed_csrf)

exec: pm.test('login page boot JSON found', () => pm.expect(m, 'no boot JSON: read the HTML error page in the response').to.not.equal(null));

request.description: Creates the Identity transaction for the id RMS generated and embeds its CSRF token.

item.name: Identity: sign in for RMS (saves core_assertion + sid)

request.description: client_id must be rms-web-dev. Run the RMS callback within 60 s.

item.name: RMS: callback with core_assertion (sets encrypted rms_session)

request.description: Verifies the assertion (JWKS RS256, iss, aud, exp, txn, jti replay) and Authorization access, then sets rms_session: JWE (dir, A256GCM) with the verified claims and the core_assertion. LOGIN_TRANSACTION_MISMATCH: the rms_login_txn cookie was not sent (check Cookies → localhost).

item.name: RMS: current user and assertion claims (GET /api/me)

exec: pm.test('assertion claims from the session cookie', () => pm.expect(b.assertion && b.assertion.aud).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('client_id')));

request.description: assertion = claims decrypted from rms_session; session.expires_at = SESSION_TTL_SECONDS. The raw core_assertion is never returned.
Calls Authorization /authorization/check with the RMS service token. Try create, edit, delete: 403 with reason when the role lacks the permission.

item.name: RMS: sign out of RMS only

request.description: Deletes the Redis session; the same rms_session cookie then gets 401 on /api/me. The federation session stays.
Ends the RMS session and returns the form (client_id, logout_hint = sid, post_logout_redirect_uri, state) the browser posts top-level to Identity /federation/logout.
Public key the Authorization service uses to verify the RMS backend service tokens.
authorization_service "up" only means the Authorization service answers /health.
